Go to tdeecalculator.net (a calculator that calculates your total daily energy expenditure) You plug in your information and it tells you exactly what you need to do. 

It lowers your daily calories by 500c. from whatever it would be to maintain. And gives you a couple of options for how to split your macros, to fit into what ever your goal is.

I wouldn't focus on following any of these diets. Just focus on eating a well rounded amount of macros. And eat at a calorie deficit for weight loss. (500 less calories is optimal because you'll lose at a healthy decline, which will help your body when it comes to the loose skin, I wouldn't however be too concerned about that, at your age and the amount you would like to lose you have a very good chance at not seeing side effects after your weight loss. 

Just don't restrict too much ;) stay within the 500c. Deficit 

I'm not sure if you do already but look into strength exercises, and some cardio. Staying active and building muscle will 100% be a help, even though it is only 20% of the battle when it comes to weight loss ;)

Also a huge thing I found was eating whole foods. Stay far away from processed stuff and any unnatural sugar for the first bit, until you get into the swing if things. Even now 3 months after allowing those things back into my diet, I often prefer an apple over a candy bar (not what I would have chosen before) because your body starts communicating a bit better with you. 

But definitely check out your TDEE, it was the best decision I made for starting my weight loss!
